proposals: The Directorate General of Shipping should publish a register of biofuel bunker suppliers holding interim and full-term certificates under Circular 32/2025, with issue dates and ports served, so whether any delivery has yet taken place under the new framework can be checked.

The Directorate General of Shipping should publish quarterly biofuel bunker volumes delivered at Indian ports, by port and blend grade, compiled from the Bunker Delivery Notes the circular already requires, so India's scale can be tracked against Singapore's roughly 0.88 million tonnes a year.

The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways should publish a quarterly status report on the Paradip green-fuel jetty, the VOC Port methanol bunkering facility and the Greenzo plant at Kandla, giving award, construction and commissioning dates, so approvals can be told apart from working infrastructure.

The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy should report how the ₹115 crore pilot outlay for green hydrogen in shipping was spent by the end of FY2025–26, by vessel retrofit and port facility, so the scheme's output can be matched to what was built.

Deendayal Port Authority should publish its Port Readiness Level assessment for bio-methanol bunkering, with the criteria it must still meet to reach level 7, so the score of 6 can be read as a checklist rather than a headline.
